## Design

### 2026-10-11 – At the beginning, i've started to download KiCad (because i'm a beginner) and then durring almost 3hours i have read and follow the path of the tuto, I'm French so understand all the English sentences

**6.5h**

At the beginning, i've started to download KiCad (because i'm a beginner) and then durring almost 3hours i have read and follow the path of the tuto, I'm French so understand all the English sentences was not really easy x)  I've learned a lot of word or expressions, such as footprints, ERC, DRC, netclass
 (know their meaning is really necessary to start the adventure) I've  then make my first schematic file,  then switch to the pcb editor. I've learned how to create a symbol and a footprint and make a link between them. I think this tuto is really important to understand the tool that you have in hands. (the link here leeds to the tuto "https://docs.kicad.org/")
I have then started to look for pieces that will match for my 8 key macropad , mechanical button to make great noise when pressing on it, like the Cherry MX, choose the Pro Micro RP2040 because it's a simple version of micro-controller to begin with, also choose diode matrices to deal with the button system (just find which item i will use took me 2 entire hours)
To finish I have started making my real schematic file for the 8 key macropad and it took me approximately (because it's more, but I have really struggled) 1 hour and 30 minutes,
